recentEventsByGoal.objective: Build a standalone single-agent durable coding-agent harness in ~/Git/pi-durable-harness (currently empty), extracted from only the harness-generic code in ~/Git/Durian-Pi, with @earendil-works/pi-durable (pinned v1.5.1, one storage opener) as the session/transcript/state backend, so an agent running this harness can re-use the pi package ecosystem: interactive TUI (pi-tui), print mode, and JSON/RPC mode matching pi's CLI surface as closely as possible, plus a best-effort pi-package compatibility layer that discovers and loads pi packages (extensions, skills, prompt templates, themes, context files) and maps pi's extension API (registerTool, commands/shortcuts, event handlers, renderers, TUI hooks) onto pi-durable's registry (defineExtension/defineTool/hook/section/wrapTool), with every unmappable pi capability named in a documented matrix rather than silently dropped. Durian-Pi's multi-seat orchestration (seats, cross-seat work queue, broker/serve, genlock, per-item worktrees, metrics, check, constitution, selfdev) is explicitly dropped. Execution protocol: a small sequential spine (task-1 pin/deps, task-2 harness core) lands first, then the module tasks (task-3..task-9) are independent siblings and are delegated concurrently to pi-native subagents, each owning disjoint files with its own verification contract (see per-task contracts). HARD RULES: (1) .mjs ESM, "type": "module", pinned @earendil-works 1.5.1 via pi-main.pin.json + scripts/sync-pi.mjs, no invented APIs - verify every pi-durable/pi-ai/chord symbol against the pinned dist .d.ts before use; (2) never reimplement harness-owned state and never run SQL of our own (one storage opener); (3) every extracted file carries a provenance header naming the Durian-Pi source path and what changed and why; (4) Durian-Pi is read-only - never modify, move, or delete anything under ~/Git/Durian-Pi; (5) GIT DISCIPLINE: the new project is a git repo from the start; commit after every landed task with a message naming the task and evidence, keep the tree clean-committed before starting a parallel subagent branch, and never rely on uncommitted state - assume progress can be lost at any moment and that anything not on disk (committed) may have to be redone; (6) nothing is claimed as working unless a runnable offline demo in the project's demo/ suite proves it. GLOBAL VERIFICATION CONTRACT before goal completion: run the full offline demo suite (0 failures, no API keys, no network); run scripts/sync-pi.mjs --report (PIN == DECLARED == RESOLVED at 1.5.1, no LOUD FALLBACK line); re-read pi's docs packages.md/extensions.md/rpc.md/cli.md/sessions.md/compaction.md and confirm each capability is either exercised by a demo id cited in docs/package-support.md or listed there as unsupported with a reason; rg confirms no dependency on the dropped orchestration concepts; git status clean in ~/Git/pi-durable-harness and unchanged in ~/Git/Durian-Pi.
